headline: There are THREE data bodies here, not two, and the third one — the translation corpus — is the only one that actually forces an architecture change. Measured at HEAD: `dist/index.html` is 7,791,592 bytes, of which the `lang/*.json` + `lang/*.data.json` dicts for just 6 languages are 5.68 MB (73%); the entire cited catalog is ~0.8 MB and `app.js`+`app.css` are 1.23 MB. The owner's fixed 23-language queue projects the single file to ~24 MB. Meanwhile the actual persistence question is boring and cheap: user state is already document-shaped, `store.get/set` (app.js:1628-1630) is a genuine two-function chokepoint with 237 call sites and only 3 direct `localStorage.setItem` leaks, so a sync layer slots underneath it without touching a single caller. My verdict: the catalog NEVER moves to a server DB (it is the offline story, the safety backbone, and the only reason DoD-10 is statically verifiable); user state needs a home but NOT a relational schema — one Durable Object per subscription, with the AI meter moved into it, serves realtime + cross-device sync + the blocked P0-worker atomicity with one mechanism. Infra cost is $5/mo at 100 subs and ~$8-10/mo at 10,000; Gemini COGS is 99% of the bill at every scale.
recommendation:
DO NOW, before/alongside CP2 — all three are pure wins, need no server, and are the "make it survive" moves (≈4 tasks total):

(A) **Write the `SYNCABLE` key manifest.** An explicit table in app.js classifying every key prefix — the ~60 literal `mk-*` keys plus the 9 dynamic families (`note:`, `rating:`, `done:cut-`, `seas:cook:`, `wpck:`, `mk-tlstate-<scope>`, `mk-menuqty-<key>`, `mk-item-cooker-<key>`, `st-<scope>-<id>`) — as `{ns, sync:'doc'|'blob'|'device-local'|'never'}`. Rewire `exportData` (app.js:7521) to read it. Today `exportData` loops ALL of localStorage and blocklists exactly one key (`mk-gemkey`); that is one new key away from leaking a secret into a shared backup, and it puts the regenerable 3000-entry `mk-mtcache` into every user's backup. This is ~1 task, improves the product today, and IS the sync schema later. **Highest leverage item in this lens.**

(B) **Close the 3 direct `localStorage.setItem` sites** (app.js:7537 importData, 8522 undo-restore, 11528 seas migration) so they route through `store`. ~0.5 task. Protects the one seam that makes everything else cheap. Right now that seam exists by luck, not design.

(C) **Split the i18n dicts out of the single file.** Emit `lang-<code>.json` from build.py instead of inlining `I18N_DICTS` (build.py:646-647), load the active language at boot, precache it in `sw.js`. ~2-3 tasks. Independent of React, independent of the server, and the ONLY thing standing between the current architecture and a 24 MB bundle. Do it before the queue passes ~10 languages, or every user in Israel downloads 22 languages they cannot read.

THEN, gated on the first paying customer (not a date):

(D) **P0-worker hardening with the meter moved into a per-subscription Durable Object** — ~3 tasks. Closes B19-B22/E14/H-3 and simultaneously creates the object sync will live in. Do NOT build the meter on KV and then move it: KV free is 1,000 writes/day with a documented 1-write-per-second-per-key ceiling, which is exactly why B21's TOCTOU exists. A DO makes the race impossible rather than unlikely.

(E) **Sync v1 on the same DO** — namespaced documents (`prefs`, `fleet`, `ev:<id>`, `journal`), DO-assigned monotonic `rev`, conditional PUT with `ifRev`, 409-returns-current-body. Photos to R2 by SHA-256. ~5-6 tasks.

(F) **Realtime via WebSocket Hibernation on the same DO** — broadcast the new `rev`, clients pull. ~2 tasks, nearly free once (E) exists; hibernated sockets accrue no duration billing, so a 12-hour cook with 2 devices attached costs essentially nothing.

(G) **Privacy notice + hard-delete path + Cloudflare DPA**, copy through `L(he,en)` and Guards A/B/C in every active language. ~2 tasks plus translation cost — and note that cost scales with the language queue, which is a real reason to sequence (C) and the queue deliberately.

Total server story: ~15-17 tasks ≈ 1.5 CP2s. That is the number to hold. It is not a rewrite.

**D1 enters only on a named trigger:** the first cross-user question you can actually name (billing reconciliation against a Paddle webhook, a support tool that finds a user by email hash). Then it holds `users(sub_id, email_hash, plan, created_at, deleted_at)` and `entitlements` — identity only, never cook data. Building a relational schema for a query nobody makes is precisely the wasted work the owner fears.

**Catalog mechanism, if CP3 volume ever justifies out-of-band updates:** bundled complete cited baseline (always) + an Ed25519-signed, append-only content pack on R2 merged into a separate `EXTRA` namespace. A pack may ADD paths/prose/citations and may NEVER alter a `safe`, `temp`, `bcheck` or duration on an existing item — enforced both by a build-time PACK_GUARD in the same family as Guards A/B/C and by a client-side field allow-list at merge. Pack missing or corrupt → the app is exactly what it is today.

survives.asset: The whole catalog + citation pipeline: data.py, sources.py, equipment_map.py, build.py Guards A/B/C. Verified: CUT_SOURCES 130 + SPEC_SOURCES 47 + MAKE_SOURCES 102 = the 279 citations, merged at build time; built payload ~0.8 MB.
survives.survivesHow: A server changes nothing about it. It stays inlined, versioned with the app, read synchronously by the engine. It is also the ONLY reason DoD-10 ("no bcheck stage, temp, safe value or cook duration altered") is statically verifiable — `bcheck` is generated from `meta.obj.safe` at app.js:4167, reading build-time inlined data. Move safety values into a server row and the DoD gate has nothing to inspect.
survives.condition: Refuse, in writing, the idea that the catalog becomes a server table. If a content-delta mechanism is ever built, it must be additive-only and safety-frozen (see recommendation).

survives.asset: The rules engine and every derived-value function: itemStages, itemPaths, effectiveSchedule, deriveRequires, planSchedule, EQM.ownership/availability/allocate/release. This is the majority of the intellectual work in the repo.
survives.survivesHow: They read the bundled catalog and user state. Neither the storage backend nor a React render layer changes their signature. They stay synchronous and offline — which sw.js:8 (`if(url.origin!==location.origin) return`) makes mandatory anyway: anything cross-origin is dead offline by the service worker's own deliberate design.
survives.condition: Never put the engine behind a network call. The user is in a yard next to a smoker for 12 hours on flaky mobile data and the answers are safety-relevant.

survives.asset: `store.get/set` (app.js:1628-1630) as the persistence chokepoint — 237 call sites across app.js + equipment.js, and only 3 direct `localStorage.setItem` leaks outside it (7537, 8522, 11528).
survives.survivesHow: This is THE seam. A sync layer slots underneath `store` without touching a single one of the 237 callers. It is also why the test fixtures survive: `seedApp(page, kv)` seeds localStorage, so as long as sync sits under `store` and localStorage stays the local source of truth, all 816 tests keep working unchanged.
survives.condition: Close the 3 direct setItem sites NOW (recommendation B), and make it a standing rule that sync never bypasses `store` and never displaces localStorage as the local source of truth. This seam exists by luck; make it exist by design.

survives.survivesHow: Becomes the onboarding path and the safety net. First sign-in on a device with existing data uploads through the same classification; first sign-in on a SECOND device exports a backup file BEFORE any destructive choice. The 'I lost my journal' fear is retired by code that already ships.
survives.condition: Rewire it to the SYNCABLE manifest (recommendation A) rather than the current loop-everything-and-blocklist-one-key shape.

survives.asset: equipment.js / EQM and the registered appjs-modularization pattern (docs/analysis/program/registered-2026-07-25-appjs-modularization.md).
survives.survivesHow: The ORCH / NAV / VOICE / AI / I18N extractions with an F5 single-definition guard per module are exactly the right preparation for any future render-layer change, and they pay off whether or not React ever happens. The document already says app.js shrinks by attrition, never big-bang. That instinct is correct and my lens reinforces it.
survives.condition: Take the I18N extraction WITH the dict-splitting work (recommendation C) — same phase, one plan, since both touch the same build.py emission and the same loader.

survives.asset: The document shape of user state itself. mk-events (app.js:9623), mk-tlstate-*, mk-eqm-ledger (equipment.js:305), mk-journal (app.js:4531) are all already opaque per-scope blobs.
survives.survivesHow: The DO SQLite schema stores them verbatim as `body TEXT`. No normalization, no ORM, no migration of the data itself — only a `rev`, an `updatedAt`, a `deviceId` and a `deleted` tombstone wrapped around what you already write.
survives.condition: Do not let anyone talk you into normalizing events into rows. A live cook is one document that changes as a unit; joins buy nothing and cost everything.

dies.asset: The single-file delivery model — IF the 23-language queue ships inline as it does today.
dies.whyLost: Measured, not projected: dist/index.html = 7,791,592 bytes with 6 languages; lang/ raw JSON for those 6 = 5,675,020 bytes (de 898K, en 791K, es 899K, fr 946K, it 903K, ru 1,238K). The arithmetic closes exactly: app.js 1.05 MB + app.css 0.18 MB + catalog ~0.8 MB + dicts 5.68 MB = 7.71 MB. Extrapolating the remaining 17 queued languages (several — ja/ko/th/hi/ar/zh — will be at or above ru's UTF-8 weight) gives ~24 MB, roughly 6.7 MB gzipped. That is not a shippable mobile PWA, and it is 73%-and-rising of a payload the user cannot read.
dies.couldWeSaveIt: YES, completely, and cheaply. Per-language JSON files emitted by build.py, the active language precached by sw.js, others fetched on switch. ~2-3 tasks. The 'single file' property is worth defending as a DEV property (one build, one artifact, one deploy) — it was never worth defending as a single HTTP response. Nothing else about the architecture changes.

dies.asset: The unclassified export loop (app.js:7521-7522) — 'iterate all of localStorage, `continue` on mk-gemkey'.
dies.whyLost: It cannot survive contact with sync: the blocklist is one newly-added secret away from leaking, and it currently ships the regenerable 3000-entry mk-mtcache in every backup.
dies.couldWeSaveIt: Not worth saving. Replace with the allow-list manifest — which is a strict improvement today, independent of sync.

dies.asset: The ad-hoc migration sentinels: mk-seas-migrated (app.js:11517), mk-inv-ver, equipMigrateFromGear() (app.js:8857). G-2 records that there is still no unified mk-schema registry, open since ROADMAP-v149.
dies.whyLost: One-shot forward-only on-device rewrites are correct for one device. With two devices at different app versions on one document they are a data-loss bug that presents as a sync bug: device A on v290 migrates `seas:`→`seas:cook:`, syncs; device B on v277 pulls keys it does not understand and writes back the old shape.
dies.couldWeSaveIt: Partly. Keep them as the local upgrade path, but add `schemaVer` to every document and have the DO refuse a write from a lower `schemaVer` with 426 Upgrade Required and a 'this device needs an update to sync' message. ~30 lines. The alternative — bidirectional migrations — is a research project and should be refused outright.

dies.asset: `mk-central-code` / the X-Access-Code bearer as an identity (G-4: 72-bit, no device binding, CORS '*' at worker/index.js:21).
dies.whyLost: A shareable code means two strangers land on the same tenant object. Fine for a dev cohort; fatal as a subscription identity.
dies.couldWeSaveIt: Not as-is. Replace with subId = HMAC(serverSecret, paddleSubscriptionId) plus a signed rotating per-device token. The dev-cohort code path can stay for BYOK/testing behind a flag.

dies.asset: Journal photos as base64 data URLs inside mk-journal (app.js:4547; downscale to 360px max, JPEG q0.6 at 4554-4560).
dies.whyLost: They are already a localStorage quota hazard (the code has an explicit catch that drops the photo and toasts 'no storage room'). Syncing them inside the document would blow the 5 GB DO SQLite ceiling at roughly 1,500 users and would make you a GDPR controller for user-generated images.
dies.couldWeSaveIt: YES — content-addressed to R2 by SHA-256, free egress, 10 GB free tier. Measured at ~20-40 KB each this is ~6 GB at 10,000 users. The on-device format need not change at all; only where the sync layer sends it.

triggers: **Language #10 enters the queue** (or dist/index.html crosses ~12 MB) → split the i18n dicts out of the bundle. Do not wait for #23; every language shipped inline before the split is work you re-verify afterwards.

**Money changes hands — the first paying subscriber exists** → P0-worker hardening with the meter in a Durable Object becomes mandatory, not optional. Until then the fail-open at worker/index.js:56 costs you your own Gemini bill; after then it costs someone else's data.

**The owner can name a cross-user question** ('how many subscribers used the orchestrator', 'find this user by email for support', 'reconcile entitlements against Paddle') → that is when D1 is justified, and only for identity/entitlements, never for cook data.

**A user asks for their data on a second device** → sync v1. Note this trigger may never fire if (A) the manifest-backed export lands first: 'export on phone, import on tablet' is a real answer for a solo hobbyist and buys you months.
**DO SQLite storage crosses 3 GB** (60% of the 5 GB ceiling) → audit what is in the document that should be in R2. This is the only hard technical wall in the whole design.

**A vendor ships OAuth or webhooks for probe telemetry** → revisit server-side IoT ingest. Until then refuse third-party credential custody as a standing policy; the app-is-closed telemetry gap is the ONE requirement that genuinely cannot be met client-side and it should be a named row in the gap map, not a vague 'we might need a backend'.

**A regulator-shaped event: first EU subscriber, or the first deletion request** → the privacy notice, DPA and hard-delete path stop being a task and become a deadline. Better to have shipped them with sync v1.

risks.risk: The 23-language queue continues shipping dicts inline and the bundle reaches 15-24 MB. Every new user pays a multi-megabyte first load for languages they cannot read; the existing cold-CWV gaps (F-6 LCP 2863, F-7 decoded 2.69 MB / ParseHTML 400ms — both measured at a much smaller bundle) get materially worse; and the F-8 whole-body MutationObserver that re-runs applyI18n/tnode/hydrateMT for every non-Hebrew user (app.js:11390) compounds it.
risks.mitigation: Split the dicts before language #10. ~2-3 tasks: build.py emits lang-<code>.json instead of substituting __I18N_DICTS__; a loader fetches the active language; sw.js precaches it; the existing tests/i18n-completeness.spec.ts leak gate is re-pointed. Guards A/B/C keep operating on the same source files and do not change at all.

risks.risk: Journal photos are synced inside the user document. At ~20-40 KB each and ~20/user/year this quietly consumes the 5 GB Durable Object SQLite ceiling at roughly 1,500 subscribers, and simultaneously makes us a GDPR/PPL controller for user-generated images with no deletion story.
risks.mitigation: Photos go to R2 by SHA-256 from day one of sync, never into the document. Make it a schema invariant (the `blobs` table exists precisely so the document holds a sha, not bytes) and assert it in a test.

risks.risk: Last-write-wins is implemented on `updatedAt` from the device clock. The app already has a documented UTC-vs-local divergence — `today()` returns a UTC date (app.js:3547), `isoDate()` returns a local date (app.js:6803), logged as B18 OPEN — so a device with a skewed clock silently wins every race and the user loses edits with no error anywhere.
risks.mitigation: Order on a DO-assigned monotonic `rev`, never on a client timestamp. Client sends `ifRev`; server returns 409 with the current body on mismatch. `updatedAt` stays as advisory display only. This is one integer and it converts LWW from a hope into a rule.

risks.risk: Tenant isolation is implemented as a predicate (a WHERE user_id = ... check, or an RLS policy) rather than as addressing. One forgotten check exposes every user's events, guest counts and journals — exactly the §9.3 defect the panel already rejected.
risks.mitigation: Make the Durable Object's identity the tenant boundary: `env.SYNC.idFromName(subId)` where subId is derived server-side from a verified subscription token. There is then no query that can cross tenants, because there is no shared table. A missing check reaches nothing instead of reaching everything. State this to the owner in exactly those terms — it is the strongest security argument for the DO shape.

risks.risk: Sync is built beside `store` rather than underneath it, or introduces its own async accessors. The 237 `store.get/set` call sites and the `seedApp(page,kv)` localStorage-seeding fixture that all 816 tests depend on both break, and the render layer starts needing loading states — which then need new user-facing strings through L() in every active language and through Guards A/B/C.
risks.mitigation: Hard architectural rule: localStorage remains the local source of truth and the ONLY synchronous read path; sync is a background reconcile beneath `store`. Nothing above `store` learns that a server exists. Write this into the sync spec as a DoD line.

risks.risk: The meter or the sync is built on KV. Free tier is 1,000 writes/day with a documented 1-write-per-second-per-key limit — the exact primitive that produces the existing TOCTOU (B21, worker/index.js:53 read / :84 write straddling an await). It works at 20 dev users and fails at 200 real ones, and then has to be rebuilt.
risks.mitigation: Put the meter in the Durable Object as part of P0-worker, not as a later migration. Debit-first inside the object's transaction. Same work, done once.

risks.risk: Privacy/consent copy is scoped as 'add a page' and then meets Guard A: every new user-facing string must exist in every active language, 6 today and 23 queued, each through Guards A/B/C. A legal-text epic arrives at the worst moment, mid-launch.
risks.mitigation: Cost the translation of privacy/consent/deletion copy INTO the sync epic from the start (my ~2-task figure for (G) assumes 6 languages; at 23 it is materially more). This is a genuine argument for deciding the language-queue sequencing and the sync timing together rather than separately.

risks.risk: Whole-store end-to-end encryption is promised as a marketing line, then a support case or a schema fix requires reading a document — and the promise has to be broken, or the user's data is unrecoverable after a forgotten passphrase.
risks.mitigation: Encrypt the `journal` namespace and the R2 photo objects client-side; leave `prefs`/`fleet`/`ev:*` server-readable. You get most of the trust story and keep the ability to repair and migrate. Be precise in the copy about what is and is not E2E — an overclaim here is worse than no claim.

effort:
Unit: one CP2-sized task (CP2 = 11 tasks / ~150 code blocks, so ~14 code blocks per task).

**Track 1 — survivability prep, do now, no server (≈4 tasks ≈ 0.35 CP2):**
- SYNCABLE key manifest + rewire exportData/importData to it — **1 task**. (~60 literal mk-* keys + 9 dynamic families to classify; one loop rewritten; the existing backup/restore tests extend.)
- Close the 3 direct localStorage.setItem sites (7537, 8522, 11528) — **0.5 task**.
- Split i18n dicts out of the bundle: build.py emits per-language JSON, boot loader, sw.js precache list, re-point the leak test — **2.5 tasks**. (Guards A/B/C are unchanged — they operate on lang/ sources, not the bundle.)

**Track 2 — the server, gated on the first paying customer (≈12-13 tasks ≈ 1.15 CP2):**
- P0-worker hardening with the meter moved into a per-subscription Durable Object: fail-closed on bad KV, debit-first inside the DO transaction, AbortController on upstream, stream-path metering, CORS lock-down, drop the hasKey leak — **3 tasks**. RED tests already exist in worker/test/index.spec.js (including the `it.fails` at :59), so the TDD RED witness is free.
- Subscription identity: Paddle webhook → subId = HMAC(secret, paddleSubId) → signed rotating device token; replace mk-central-code — **1.5 tasks**.
- Sync v1: 4-table DO SQLite schema (docs/blobs/cursor/meter), namespaced documents, rev + ifRev conditional PUT, 409-with-body, tombstones, schemaVer refusal — **4 tasks**.
- Photos to R2 by SHA-256 + the client upload/fetch path — **1 task**.
- Onboarding: first-sync-is-an-import, export-before-any-destructive-choice on the second device — **1 task** (reuses exportData).
- Realtime: WebSocket Hibernation on the same DO, broadcast rev, client pulls — **1.5 tasks**.
- Privacy notice + hard delete (DO deleteAll + R2 delete + tombstone) + DPA + copy through L() and Guards A/B/C — **2 tasks at 6 languages**; materially more at 23, which is why (C) and the language queue should be sequenced together.

**Total: ~16-17 tasks ≈ 1.5 CP2s for the complete server story, spread across two gated tracks.**

**What is NOT in that number, deliberately:** any React work, any D1 schema, any catalog migration, any change to the rules engine, any change to the 279-citation pipeline, and any change to the 816-test suite's assertions. That is the honest answer to "if the outcome is a rewrite, the work is wasted" — on this lens, nothing is a rewrite. The persistence change is ~1.5 CP2s of NEW code sitting underneath a two-function seam that already exists, and the single-file bundle problem (~3 tasks) is the only thing that is genuinely urgent, and it has nothing to do with React or with a server at all.
openQuestions: **What exactly does 'realtime sync' mean — MY devices, or MY GUESTS' devices?** 'My phone and my tablet see the same live cook' is single-user LWW on a document and is ~5-6 tasks. 'My eight guests watch the timeline' is fan-out to untrusted readers, needs a share token, a read-only projection, and different privacy copy. The panel asked this and it is still unanswered. My whole design assumes the first. Please answer before anything is built.

**Is the 23-language queue committed to shipping inline in the bundle?** If yes, the single-file property is gone at ~24 MB and we should say so out loud now. If it may become per-language fetches, the property survives in every sense that matters (one build, one artifact, one deploy) and the problem disappears for ~3 tasks. This is the most consequential open question in this lens.

**Are you willing to be a data controller for user photos?** They are stored on-device today (app.js:4547) and that is a materially different legal position from holding them. Options: (a) sync photos to R2 as a controller, with a DPA and deletion path; (b) client-side-encrypt the journal namespace and photos so we hold ciphertext we cannot read — cheaper legally, but a forgotten passphrase is total loss for that user and we can never repair it; (c) do not sync photos at all in v1. I lean (b) for journal+photos and server-readable for everything else.

**Does the FREE / BYOK tier sync?** If yes, a Durable Object exists for every non-paying user — still cheap (the free plan supports SQLite-backed DOs and hibernated sockets do not accrue duration billing), but it weakens the '04b' business argument that sync is the paid hook. If no, the free tier keeps localStorage + manifest-backed export, which is a genuinely decent product on its own.

**Would a manifest-backed export/import (export on the phone, import on the tablet) satisfy the multi-device need well enough to DELAY sync behind CP2 → E4 → CP3?** It is ~1 task versus ~13, it is zero infrastructure, zero legal exposure, and it retires the 'I lost my journal' fear immediately. If the answer is yes, that reorders the entire roadmap in the owner's favour.

**Is probe telemetry while the app is CLOSED a committed feature?** It is the only requirement anywhere in the programme that genuinely cannot be met client-side, and it is currently missing from the 141-gap map entirely. If committed, it is an independent reason to have a server and should be scoped; if not, user-initiated file import plus a manual-override button deliver most of the value with zero infrastructure — and we should refuse third-party credential custody as a standing policy either way.

**MAKES count discrepancy, minor but worth resolving:** build.py's own print reports 279 tagged recipes (130 CUTS + 47 SPECIALS + 102 MAKES) and MAKE_SOURCES has 102 entries, but importing data.py directly yields MAKES = 50. Something expands MAKES between data.py and the build (sausages_new.py, most likely). It does not change any conclusion here — the citation count of 279 is verified directly — but a build assertion pinning the recipe count would be a cheap addition to the P4 build-assertions work that is already open.
